title: Find Second Largest Element
problemStatement: Given an array of integers `arr`, write a function `findSecondLargest(arr)` that returns the second largest element in the array. If no such element exists (e.g. all elements are equal or the array has fewer than 2 distinct values), return -1.
description: The array can contain duplicate values. The second largest must be strictly smaller than the largest value.
constraints:
1 <= arr.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: A single integer — the second largest element, or -1 if it does not exist.

examples.explanation: The largest element is 35 and the second largest is 34.
All elements are equal, so there is no second largest element.

explanation: Track the largest and second largest values in a single pass. If every value equals the largest, return -1.

title: Sum of Prime Digits
problemStatement: Given a number represented as a string `numStr`, write a function `sumOfPrimeDigits(numStr)` that returns the sum of all digits which are prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7). Non-prime digits are ignored.
description: Treat the input purely as a string of digits. The result is the sum of the digit values 2, 3, 5 and 7 wherever they appear.
constraints:
1 <= numStr.length <= 10^5
numStr contains only digits '0'-'9'
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)
inputFormat: A single string containing digits only.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of the prime digits.

examples.explanation: None of the digits are prime, so the sum is 0.

explanation: Iterate over each character, convert it to an integer, and add it to the total only if it is 2, 3, 5 or 7.

title: Reverse Words in a String
problemStatement: Given an input string `s`, write a function `reverseWords(s)` that reverses the order of the words. A word is a sequence of non-space characters. Words in `s` are separated by at least one space. Return the words in reverse order joined by a single space.
description: Leading and trailing spaces are ignored, and multiple spaces between words are collapsed into one in the output.
constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10^4
s contains printable ASCII characters and spaces
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
outputFormat: A single string with words reversed and separated by a single space.

examples.explanation: The words are reversed in order: blue, is, sky, the.
Extra spaces are trimmed from both ends and between words.

explanation: Split the string on whitespace, filter out empty tokens, reverse the list and join with a single space.
